verses.zh: 使徒对百姓说话的时候，祭司们和守殿官，并撒都该人忽然来了。
verses.en: While Peter and John[NOTE:1] were speaking to the people, the priests and the commander[NOTE:2] of the temple guard[NOTE:3] and the Sadducees[NOTE:4] came up[NOTE:5] to them,
notes: Grk “While they”; the referents (Peter and John) have been specified in the translation for clarity.
Or “captain.”

The commander of the temple guard was the title of the officer commanding the Jewish soldiers responsible for guarding and keeping order in the temple courts in Jerusalem.tn Grk “the official of the temple,” a title for the commander of the Jewish soldiers guarding the temple (thus the translation, “the commander of the temple guard”). See L&N 37.91.

The Sadducees controlled the official political structures of Judaism at this time, being the majority members of the Sanhedrin. They were known as extremely strict on law and order issues (Josephus, J. W. 2.8.2 [2.119], 2.8.14 [2.164-166]; Ant. 13.5.9 [13.171-173], 13.10.6 [13.293-298], 18.1.2 [18.11], 18.1.4 [18.16-17], 20.9.1 [20.199]; Life 2 [10-11]). See also Matt 3:7; 16:1-12; 22:23-34; Mark 12:18-27; Luke 20:27-38; Acts 5:17; 23:6-8.
Or “approached.” This verb often denotes a sudden appearing (BDAG 418 s.v. ἐφίστημι 1).

verses.zh: 因他们教训百姓，本着耶稣，传说死人复活，就很烦恼，
verses.en: angry[NOTE:1] because they were teaching the people and announcing[NOTE:2] in Jesus the resurrection of the dead.
notes: Or “greatly annoyed,” “provoked.”
Or “proclaiming.”

verses.zh: 于是下手拿住他们；因为天已经晚了，就把他们押到第二天。
verses.en: So[NOTE:1] they seized[NOTE:2] them and put them in jail[NOTE:3] until the next day (for it was already evening).
notes: Grk “And” Here καί (kai) has been translated as “so” to indicate the logical sequence of events.
Or “they arrested”; Grk “they laid hands on.”
Or “prison,” “custody.”

verses.zh: 但听道之人有许多信的，男丁数目约到五千。
verses.en: But many of those who had listened to[NOTE:1] the message[NOTE:2] believed, and the number of the men[NOTE:3] came to about 5,000.
notes: Or “had heard.”
Or “word.”

In the historical setting it is likely that only men are referred to here. The Greek term ἀνήρ (anēr) usually refers to males or husbands rather than people in general. Thus to translate “of the people” would give a false impression of the number, since any women and children were apparently not included in the count.

verses.zh: 第二天，官府、长老，和文士在耶路撒冷聚会，
verses.en: On the next day,[NOTE:1] their rulers, elders, and experts in the law[NOTE:2] came together[NOTE:3] in Jerusalem.[NOTE:4]
notes: Grk “It happened that on the next day.” The introductory phrase ἐγένετο (egeneto, “it happened that”), common in Luke (69 times) and Acts (54 times), is redundant in contemporary English and has not been translated.

Experts in the law would have been mostly like the Pharisees in approach. Thus various sects of Judaism were coming together against Jesus.tn Or “and scribes.” The traditional rendering of γραμματεύς (grammateus) as “scribe” does not communicate much to the modern English reader, for whom the term might mean “professional copyist,” if it means anything at all. The people referred to here were recognized experts in the law of Moses and in traditional laws and regulations. Thus “expert in the law” comes closer to the meaning for the modern reader.
Or “law assembled,” “law met together.”
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 又有大祭司亚那和该亚法、约翰、亚历山大，并大祭司的亲族都在那里，
verses.en: Annas the high priest was there, and Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and others who were members of the high priest’s family.[NOTE:1]
notes: The high priest’s family. This family controlled the high priesthood as far back as a.d. 6. Annas, Caiaphas, and Alexander were all high priests at one time (though Alexander held that office after this event).

verses.zh: 叫使徒站在当中，就问他们说：「你们用甚么能力，奉谁的名做这事呢？」
verses.en: After[NOTE:1] making Peter and John[NOTE:2] stand in their midst, they began to inquire, “By what power or by what name[NOTE:3] did you do this?”
notes: Grk “And after.” Because of the length and complexity of the Greek sentence, καί (kai) has not been translated here. Instead a new sentence is begun in the translation at the beginning of v. 7.
Grk “making them”; the referents (Peter and John) have been specified in the translation for clarity.
By what name. The issue of the “name” comes up again here. This question, meaning “by whose authority,” surfaces an old dispute (see Luke 20:1-8). Who speaks for God about the ancient faith?

verses.zh: 那时彼得被圣灵充满，对他们说：
verses.en: Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit,[NOTE:1] replied,[NOTE:2] “Rulers of the people and elders,[NOTE:3]
notes: Filled with the Holy Spirit. The narrator’s remark about the Holy Spirit indicates that Peter speaks as directed by God and for God. This fulfills Luke 12:11-12 (1 Pet 3:15).
Grk “Spirit, said to them.”

The Western and Byzantine texts, as well as one or two Alexandrian witnesses, read τοῦ ᾿Ισραήλ (tou Israēl, “of Israel”) after πρεσβύτεροι (presbuteroi, “elders”; so D E Ψ 33 1739 M it), while most of the better witnesses, chiefly Alexandrian (P74 א A B 0165 1175 vg sa bo), lack this modifier. The longer reading was most likely added by scribes to give literary balance to the addressees in that “Rulers” already had an adjunct while “elders” was left absolute.

verses.zh: 「治民的官府和长老啊，倘若今日因为在残疾人身上所行的善事查问我们他是怎么得了痊愈，
verses.en: if[NOTE:1] we are being examined[NOTE:2] today for a good deed[NOTE:3] done to a sick man—by what means this man was healed[NOTE:4]—
notes: This clause is a first class condition. It assumes for the sake of argument that this is what they were being questioned about.
Or “questioned.” The Greek term ἀνακρίνω (anakrinō) points to an examination similar to a legal one.
Or “for an act of kindness.”
Or “delivered” (σέσωται [sesōtai], from σώζω [sōzō]). See 4:12.

verses.zh: 你们众人和以色列百姓都当知道，站在你们面前的这人得痊愈是因你们所钉十字架、　神叫他从死里复活的拿撒勒人耶稣基督的名。
verses.en: let it be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel that by the name of Jesus Christ[NOTE:1] the Nazarene whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead, this man stands before you healthy.
notes: Or “Messiah”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”

verses.zh: 他是你们匠人所弃的石头，已成了房角的头块石头。
verses.en: This Jesus[NOTE:1] is the stone that was rejected by you,[NOTE:2] the builders, that has become the cornerstone.[NOTE:3]
notes: Grk “This one”; the referent (Jesus) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

The word “you” is inserted into the quotation because Peter is making a direct application of Ps 118:22 to his hearers. Because it is not in the OT, it has been left as normal type (rather than bold italic). The remarks are like Acts 2:22-24 and 3:12-15.
A quotation from Ps 118:22 which combines the theme of rejection with the theme of God’s vindication/exaltation.

verses.zh: 除他以外，别无拯救；因为在天下人间，没有赐下别的名，我们可以靠着得救。」
verses.en: And there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among people[NOTE:1] by which we must[NOTE:2] be saved.”
notes: Here ἀνθρώποις (anthrōpois) has been translated as a generic noun (“people”).
Must be saved. The term used here (δεῖ, dei, “it is necessary”) reflects the necessity set up by God’s directive plan.

verses.zh: 他们见彼得、约翰的胆量，又看出他们原是没有学问的小民，就希奇，认明他们是跟过耶稣的；
verses.en: When they saw the boldness[NOTE:1] of Peter and John, and discovered[NOTE:2] that they were uneducated[NOTE:3] and ordinary[NOTE:4] men, they were amazed and recognized these men had been with Jesus.
notes: Or “courage.”
Or “and found out.”

Uneducated does not mean “illiterate,” that is, unable to read or write. Among Jews in NT times there was almost universal literacy, especially as the result of widespread synagogue schools. The term refers to the fact that Peter and John had no formal rabbinic training and thus, in the view of their accusers, were not qualified to expound the law or teach publicly. The objection is like Acts 2:7.
For the translation of ἰδιῶται (idiōtai) as “ordinary men” see L&N 27.26.

verses.zh: 又看见那治好了的人和他们一同站着，就无话可驳。
verses.en: And because they saw the man who had been healed standing with them, they had nothing to say against this.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “nothing to say in opposition.”

verses.zh: 于是吩咐他们从公会出去，就彼此商议说：
verses.en: But when they had ordered them to go outside the council,[NOTE:1] they began to confer with one another,
notes: Or “the Sanhedrin” (the highest legal, legislative, and judicial body among the Jews).

verses.zh: 「我们当怎样办这两个人呢？因为他们诚然行了一件明显的神迹，凡住耶路撒冷的人都知道，我们也不能说没有。
verses.en: saying, “What should we do with these men? For it is plain[NOTE:1] to all who live in Jerusalem that a notable miraculous sign[NOTE:2] has come about through them,[NOTE:3] and we cannot deny it.
notes: Or “evident.”

Here σημεῖον (sēmeion) has been translated as “miraculous sign” rather than simply “sign” or “miracle” since both components appear to be present in the context. It is clear that the healing of the lame man was a miracle, but for the Sanhedrin it was the value of the miraculous healing as a sign that concerned them because it gave attestation to the message of Peter and John. The sign “speaks” as Peter claimed in 3:11-16.
Or “has been done by them.”

verses.zh: 惟恐这事越发传扬在民间，我们必须恐吓他们，叫他们不再奉这名对人讲论。」
verses.en: But to keep this matter from spreading any further among the people, let us warn them to speak no more[NOTE:1] to anyone in this name.”
notes: Or “speak no longer.”

verses.zh: 于是叫了他们来，禁止他们总不可奉耶稣的名讲论教训人。
verses.en: And they called them in and ordered[NOTE:1] them not to speak or teach at all in the name[NOTE:2] of Jesus.
notes: Or “commanded.”
In the name of Jesus. Once again, the “name” reflects the person. The person of Jesus and his authority is the “troubling” topic that, as far as the Jewish leadership is concerned, needs controlling.

verses.zh: 彼得、约翰说：「听从你们，不听从神，这在　神面前合理不合理，你们自己酌量吧！
verses.en: But Peter and John replied,[NOTE:1] “Whether it is right before God to obey[NOTE:2] you rather than God, you decide,
notes: Grk “answered and said to them.”
Grk “hear,” but the idea of “hear and obey” or simply “obey” is frequently contained in the Greek verb ἀκούω (akouō; see L&N 36.14).

verses.zh: 我们所看见所听见的，不能不说。」
verses.en: for it is impossible[NOTE:1] for us not to speak about what we have seen and heard.”
notes: Grk “for we are not able not to speak about what we have seen and heard,” but the double negative, which cancels out in English, is emphatic in Greek. The force is captured somewhat by the English translation “it is impossible for us not to speak…” although this is slightly awkward.

verses.zh: 官长为百姓的缘故，想不出法子刑罚他们，又恐吓一番，把他们释放了。这是因众人为所行的奇事都归荣耀与　神。
verses.en: After threatening them further, they released them, for they could not find how to punish them on account of the people, because they were all praising[NOTE:1] God for what had happened.
notes: Or “glorifying.”

verses.zh: 原来藉着神迹医好的那人有四十多岁了。
verses.en: For the man, on whom this miraculous sign[NOTE:1] of healing had been performed,[NOTE:2] was over forty years old.
notes: Here σημεῖον (sēmeion) has been translated as “miraculous sign” rather than simply “sign” or “miracle” since both components appear to be present in the context. See also the note on this word in v. 16.
Or “had been done.”

verses.zh: 二人既被释放，就到会友那里去，把祭司长和长老所说的话都告诉他们。
verses.en: When they were released, Peter and John[NOTE:1] went to their fellow believers[NOTE:2] and reported everything the high priests and the elders had said to them.
notes: Grk “they”; the referents (Peter and John) have been specified in the translation for clarity, since a new topic begins in v. 23 and the last specific reference to Peter and John in the Greek text is in 4:19.

Grk “to their own [people].” In context this phrase is most likely a reference to other believers rather than simply their own families and/or homes, since the group appears to act with one accord in the prayer that follows in v. 24. At the literary level, this phrase suggests how Jews were now splitting into two camps, pro-Jesus and anti-Jesus.

verses.zh: 他们听见了，就同心合意地高声向　神说：「主啊！你是造天、地、海，和其中万物的，
verses.en: When they heard this, they raised their voices to God with one mind[NOTE:1] and said, “Master of all,[NOTE:2] you who made the heaven, the earth,[NOTE:3] the sea, and everything that is in them,
notes: With one mind. Cf. Acts 1:14.
Or “Lord of all.”sn The use of the title Master of all (δεσπότης, despotēs) emphasizes that there is a sovereign God who is directing what is taking place.

Grk “and the earth, and the sea,” but καί (kai) has not been translated before “the earth” and “the sea” since contemporary English normally uses a coordinating conjunction only between the last two elements in a series of three or more.

verses.zh: 你曾藉着圣灵，托你仆人―我们祖宗大卫的口，说：外邦为甚么争闹？万民为甚么谋算虚妄的事？
verses.en: who said by the Holy Spirit through[NOTE:1] your servant David our forefather,[NOTE:2] ‘Why do the nations[NOTE:3] rage,[NOTE:4] and the peoples plot foolish[NOTE:5] things?
notes: Grk “by the mouth of” (an idiom).
Or “ancestor”; Grk “father.”
Or “Gentiles.”
The Greek word translated rage includes not only anger but opposition, both verbal and nonverbal. See L&N 88.185.
Or “futile”; traditionally, “vain.”

verses.zh: 世上的君王一齐起来，臣宰也聚集，要敌挡主，并主的受膏者（或译：基督）。
verses.en: The kings of the earth stood together,[NOTE:1] and the rulers assembled together,against the Lord and against his[NOTE:2] Christ.’[NOTE:3]
notes: Traditionally, “The kings of the earth took their stand.”
See the note on Christ in 2:31.tn Or “Messiah”; both “Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew and Aramaic) mean “one who has been anointed.”
A quotation from Ps 2:1-2.

verses.zh: 希律和本丢•彼拉多，外邦人和以色列民，果然在这城里聚集，要攻打你所膏的圣仆（仆：或译子）耶稣，
verses.en: “For indeed both Herod and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles and the people of Israel, assembled together in this city against[NOTE:1] your holy servant Jesus, whom you anointed,[NOTE:2]
notes: The application of Ps 2:1-2 is that Jews and Gentiles are opposing Jesus. The surprise of the application is that Jews are now found among the enemies of God’s plan.
A wordplay on “Christ,” v. 26, which means “one who has been anointed.”

verses.zh: 成就你手和你意旨所预定必有的事。
verses.en: to do as much as your power[NOTE:1] and your plan[NOTE:2] had decided beforehand[NOTE:3] would happen.
notes: Grk “hand,” here a metaphor for God’s strength or power or authority.
Or “purpose,” “will.”

Or “had predestined.” Since the term “predestine” is something of a technical theological term, not in wide usage in contemporary English, the translation “decide beforehand” was used instead (see L&N 30.84). God’s direction remains as the major theme.

verses.zh: 他们恐吓我们，现在求主鉴察，一面叫你仆人大放胆量讲你的道，一面伸出你的手来医治疾病，并且使神迹奇事因着你圣仆（仆：或译子）耶稣的名行出来。」
verses.en: And now, Lord, pay attention to[NOTE:1] their threats, and grant[NOTE:2] to your servants[NOTE:3] to speak your message[NOTE:4] with great courage,[NOTE:5]
notes: Or “Lord, take notice of.”

Grant to your servants to speak your message with great courage. The request is not for a stop to persecution or revenge on the opponents, but for boldness (great courage) to carry out the mission of proclaiming the message of what God is doing through Jesus.
Grk “slaves.” See the note on the word “servants” in 2:18.
Grk “word.”
Or “with all boldness.”

verses.zh: a
verses.en: while you extend your hand to heal, and to bring about miraculous signs[NOTE:1] and wonders through the name of your holy servant Jesus.”
notes: The miraculous nature of these signs is implied in the context.

verses.zh: 祷告完了，聚会的地方震动，他们就都被圣灵充满，放胆讲论　神的道。
verses.en: When[NOTE:1] they had prayed, the place where they were assembled together was shaken,[NOTE:2] and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak[NOTE:3] the word of God[NOTE:4] courageously.[NOTE:5]
notes: Grk “And when.” Because of the difference between Greek style, which often begins sentences or clauses with “and,” and English style, which generally does not, καί (kai) has not been translated here.
The place where they were assembled…was shaken. This signifies that God is in their midst. See Acts 16:26; Exod 19:18; Ps 114:7; Isa 6:4.

The imperfect verb has been translated as an ingressive imperfect (“began to speak”). Logical sequencing suggests that their speaking began after they were filled with the Spirit. The prayer was answered immediately.
Or “speak God’s message.”
Or “with boldness.”

verses.zh: 那许多信的人都是一心一意的，没有一人说他的东西有一样是自己的，都是大家公用。
verses.en: The group of those who believed were of one heart and mind,[NOTE:1] and no one said that any of his possessions was his own, but everything was held in common.[NOTE:2]
notes: Grk “soul.”

Everything was held in common. The remark is not a reflection of political philosophy, but of the extent of their spontaneous commitment to one another. Such a response does not have the function of a command, but is reflective of an attitude that Luke commends as evidence of their identification with one another.tn Grk “but all things were to them in common.”

verses.zh: 使徒大有能力，见证主耶稣复活；众人也都蒙大恩。
verses.en: With[NOTE:1] great power the apostles were giving testimony[NOTE:2] to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and great grace was on them all.
notes: Grk “And with.” Because of the difference between Greek style, which often begins sentences or clauses with “and,” and English style, which generally does not, καί (kai) has not been translated here.
Or “were witnessing.”

verses.zh: 内中也没有一个缺乏的；因为人人将田产房屋都卖了，
verses.en: For there was no one needy[NOTE:1] among them because those who were owners of land or houses were selling[NOTE:2] them[NOTE:3] and bringing the proceeds from the sales
notes: Or “poor.”
Grk “houses, selling them were bringing.” The participle πωλοῦντες (pōlountes) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
The word “them” is not in the Greek text, but is implied. Direct objects were often omitted in Greek when clear from the context, but must be supplied for the modern English reader.

verses.zh: 把所卖的价银拿来，放在使徒脚前，照各人所需用的，分给各人。
verses.en: and placing them at the apostles’ feet. The proceeds[NOTE:1] were distributed to each, as anyone had need.
notes: Grk “It” (or “They,” plural). The referent of the understood pronoun subject, the proceeds from the sales, of the verb διεδίδετο (diedideto) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 有一个利未人，生在塞浦路斯，名叫约瑟，使徒称他为巴拿巴（巴拿巴翻出来就是劝慰子）。
verses.en: So Joseph, a Levite who was a native of Cyprus, called by the apostles Barnabas (which is translated “son of encouragement”),[NOTE:1]
notes: This is a parenthetical note by the author. Note how the actions of Barnabas are in keeping with the meaning of his nickname. He stands in contrast to Ananias and Sapphira in 5:1-11.

verses.zh: 他有田地，也卖了，把价银拿来，放在使徒脚前。
verses.en: sold[NOTE:1] a field[NOTE:2] that belonged to him and brought the money[NOTE:3] and placed it at the apostles’ feet.
notes: Grk “selling a field that belonged to him, brought” The participle πωλήσας (pōlēsas) has been translated as a finite verb due to requirements of contemporary English style.
Or “a farm.”
Normally a reference to actual coins (“currency”). See L&N 6.68.
